tx.t: In this lecture I will describe the world's rainforests and why scientists want to protect them. Rainforests cover only about six per cent of the Earth's land surface.
However, they are home to more than half of all the plant and animal species on land. The Amazon is the largest rainforest, and it spreads across nine countries.
A rainforest has four main layers: the emergent layer, the canopy, the understorey and the forest floor. Most animals live in the canopy, where there is plenty of light and fruit.
Many modern medicines come from rainforest plants, and scientists believe thousands more are still unknown.

tx.t: Today I would like to describe a bike-sharing scheme in the town of Fenwick. It began in twenty fourteen with one hundred and seventy-four bikes, placed at stations around the centre.
Use grew quickly. Within three years the number of journeys had risen by thirty-one per cent, and on a busy day there were more than twenty-four thousand trips.
The scheme soon met a serious problem: too few bikes in the hills. The council solved it with a van that moves bikes uphill every morning.
Today, a ride costs one pounds thirty for the first half hour, and the first fifteen minutes are free for residents.

tx.t: Today I would like to talk about the Silk Road, one of the greatest trade networks in history. It was not a single road but a network of routes connecting China with the Mediterranean.
The main routes were more than six thousand kilometres long. The Chinese envoy Zhang Qian travelled west around one hundred and thirty BC and helped to open the routes.

Cities such as Samarkand and Bukhara, in what is now Uzbekistan, became rich and famous centres of trade. Besides silk, merchants carried spices, paper, glass and precious stones, and also ideas and religions.

tx.t: Today I would like to talk about the history of the Olympic Games. The ancient Games began in seven hundred and seventy-six BC at Olympia in Greece.

Women first took part in the Games in nineteen hundred, in Paris. The first Winter Games were held in nineteen twenty-four at Chamonix, in France.
Today, thousands of athletes from more than two hundred countries compete in the summer Games.
